why: The student writes the range the maths way, 5 < n < 10, which is not legal Java, and keeps the !( ). So no De Morgan rewrite happens and the rule used contradicts Java.

concepts.quote: You could write b as !(5 < n < 10).
concepts.why: The !( ) is not moved inside, the terms are not negated and && is not turned into ||. This is a maths-style rewrite, not De Morgan.
The answer makes no claim about variables.
The answer makes no claim about how &&, || or ! work.
The answer makes no claim about assignment.
The answer makes no general claim about expressions.
This is maths range notation. In Java 5 < n gives a boolean, so 5 < n < 10 does not compile and the two tests must be joined with &&.
